pages.title: About Koori
pages.content:
Koori Cold Stores opened in 1987, when Jonas Ekdahl fitted two rooms on Quay 3 at Northmere Port. The rooms were numbered from the first week, so a shipper knew which door, which band and which probe reading belonged to the goods.

In 2009 the store was rebuilt. Rooms 6 to 12 were added, together with an ammonia and CO₂ plant. Marit Ekdahl has run the store since 2016. Across twelve rooms there are 6,400 pallet positions, and eight dock doors with seals serve Quay 3, 18 Saltmarsh Road, Northmere Port.

pages.title: Ask about capacity
pages.content:
Tell us the band, the number of pallets, the weeks and the first delivery date. We reply within one working day with a room number, the positions, the start date and the rate. The offer is held for 48 hours.

Call 010 377 4120, Monday to Friday 08:00 to 17:00, or write to ask@koori-coldstore.example.

pages.title: Room alerts
pages.content:
When a room in your band frees up, we send one short email, and at most twice a month. Nothing else is sent. Mention the band you want: chilled, frozen or deep frozen.

Write to ask@koori-coldstore.example with the band in the subject line and we will add you to the list.

posts.title: Why we log every room every 10 minutes
posts.excerpt: A reading every 10 minutes, around the clock, filed against the room number.
posts.content:
Every room at Koori is read every 10 minutes, day and night. The reading is filed against the room number, so the weekly log, sent as a PDF and a CSV, shows one line per reading for the room your pallets sit in.

The first reading is taken by the dock supervisor at the seal, when the pallet arrives. If a room leaves its band, the customer is called within 15 minutes. That is the whole reason for the ten-minute interval: it is short enough to catch a drift before it matters.

posts.title: What a 48-hour room offer means
posts.excerpt: A room offer names the room, the positions, the start date and the rate, and it is held for 48 hours.
posts.content:
Within one working day of an enquiry, Lucía Ferraz sends a room offer: the room number, the positions, the start date and the rate. The offer is held for 48 hours, which gives you time to sign the storage order and to book the first 30-minute dock slot.

If the 48 hours pass, the room goes back on the register. Nothing is charged for an offer that is not confirmed.

posts.title: Room 12 is back in the deep-frozen band
posts.excerpt: Room 12 has returned to service at −25 to −28 °C after its scheduled coil defrost.
posts.content:
Room 12 returned to service this week after its scheduled coil defrost. It holds the deep-frozen band, −25 to −28 °C, together with Room 11, which gives 900 positions for fish, seafood and ice cream.

Henrik Valo checked the plant on the morning of the return, and Aiyana Brooks confirmed the first full day of readings in the log before any pallet was put away.
